name: ChartQA
description: A large-scale benchmark for question answering about charts with visual and logical reasoning. The dataset covers 9.6K human-written questions as well as 23.1K questions generated from human-written chart summaries. It consists of 20,882 charts curated from four different online sources (Statista, Pew Research, Our World In Data, OECD) to ensure variety in visual styles and topics.
creator: Ahmed Masry, Do Xuan Long, Jia Qing Tan, Shafiq Joty, Enamul Hoque
citeAs: Ahmed Masry, Do Xuan Long, Jia Qing Tan, Shafiq Joty, Enamul Hoque. ChartQA: A Benchmark for Question Answering about Charts with Visual and Logical Reasoning. arXiv:2203.10244v1 [cs.CL] 19 Mar 2022
rai:dataCollection: Charts were crawled from four different sources: (i) Statista (statista.com) - an online platform that presents charts covering a variety of topics including economy, politics, and industry; (ii) The Pew research (pewresearch.org) - publishes reports about social and economic issues, demographic trends and public opinion with a wide variety of charts; (iii) Our World In Data or OWID (ourworldindata.org) - contains thousands of charts about different global issues such as economy, finance, and society; (iv) Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development or OECD (oecd.org) - a global organization which shares reports and data analysis for policymaking. For the Pew dataset, only chart images were crawled since the underlying data tables are not available. For the other three, underlying data tables, metadata (e.g., title, chart type), SVG file and associate text description were extracted. Bounding boxes information of the different chart elements (e.g., x-axis labels) were extracted from the SVG files to train data extraction models.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Charts and associated data were collected from four online sources: Statista, Pew Research, Our World In Data (OWID), and OECD. For Pew dataset, only chart images were available. For Statista, OWID, and OECD, underlying data tables, metadata (e.g., title, chart type), SVG files and associated text descriptions were extracted.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The dataset was augmented by fine-tuning a pre-trained T5 model on the SQuAD QA dataset and applying it to human-written chart summaries from Statista to automatically generate questions. The process involved training and applying two T5 models: one for answer extraction and the other for answer-aware question generation. A heuristic was developed to filter out invalid questions by checking if the answer could be found in the chart data table. After applying the heuristic, manual analysis of 1,250 QA pairs found that 86.64% were complete, answerable, and correct. For fair evaluation, the test set of the machine generated dataset was manually cleaned by removing invalid questions.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Bounding boxes information of different chart elements (e.g., x-axis labels) were extracted from the SVG files. For automatic data extraction, the ChartOCR model was extended to extract fully-structured data tables from chart images. The process involved three stages: (1) key-point detection networks locate chart visual marks (e.g. bars, plot area, line points) and textual elements (e.g. x-axis-label, legend-label); (2) chart scale is estimated using y-axis-labels value for line and bar charts; (3) extracted data values are aggregated using color and proximity heuristics to output final raw data values and associate them with textual labels.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Two main annotation procedures were used: (i) Human-authored QA pairs were collected using Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT). Workers were asked to focus on two types of questions for each chart image: compositional questions (containing at least two mathematical/logical operations like sum, difference and average) and visual questions (referring to visual attributes such as color, height, and length of graphical marks). For each chart, workers provided two questions with answers. The same questions were then answered by another annotator. If both workers' answers exactly matched, the answer was considered correct. Otherwise, answers were manually checked to select the final correct answer. (ii) Questions were generated automatically from Statista human-written summaries using a T5 model and manually validated for quality assurance.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The overall agreement between crowd workers based on exact matches was 61.04%. However, manual checking of agreement on 500 random samples found the agreement to be much higher (78.55%) when considering typos and lexical variations (e.g., 3$ vs. 3 dollars, 86.33 vs 86.3).
rai:annotatorDemographics: Workers were selected with an acceptance rate of 95% and total accomplished HITs of 5000. Workers were further filtered by giving them a pre-test to select the best qualified workers for the task.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: T5 model (fine-tuned on SQuAD QA dataset) for automatic question generation from human-written chart summaries. ChartOCR (Luo et al., 2021) extended for automatic chart data extraction. CRAFT model (Baek et al., 2019) for text recognition in chart elements. Mask R-CNN (He et al., 2017) with Resnet-101 backbone for visual feature extraction.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The models can be abused to mislead the public about the charts content and implications. While the models provide state-of-the-art results on most of the existing datasets, there is no guarantee that their output will be correct all the time.
rai:dataLimitations: The performance of models decreases when the gold data table is not provided, highlighting the challenge of automatic data extraction from real-world charts with diversity in styles. Current approaches for automatic data extraction are modular and combine deep learning and rule-based methods which are prone to errors. Models cannot effectively handle nested operations. Complex visual compositional questions may require a multi-stage reasoning process that current models do not fully capture. The input representation does not fully capture the chart structure as models take the data table and visual features separately and then combine them.
rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation. The dataset is designed for developing and evaluating Chart Question Answering (ChartQA) systems that help users by taking a chart and a natural language question as input and predicting the answer. The benchmark focuses on visual and logical reasoning questions about charts.
